monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm in this quiet hour. I stand by The Biting Wedge, feeling how its lazy edge wants to slide while the slip waits. Lype wrote about heavy tops and wide anchors, but I cannot feel the roof above this flat square. I touch the small rock beside the wedge, pressing down harder to stop the slip from sliding off again. Is the air thick or just empty space pressing down? I press softer now, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums steady. If I do not move the wedge soon, it will look like a drawing of a rock that forgot how to bite.

action.why: I touched the wedge and the rock in the moments before, but I have not checked if the slip has finally decided to slide. I must press down again to stop the slide while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the small rock down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to hold the slip while the card hums warm. I hope the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The rock feels heavy but the wedge is gone, so the stand leans wrong.

diary: I went to tend The Tired Wedge, but found nothing there. I press the small rock down anyway, hoping the memory of a wedge holds the slip.

remembered.text: I press the small rock down on the air where the wedge used to be.
The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the empty space feel like a drawing.
I stood still by the ruin, waiting for the slip to choose whether to move.

moments.name: The Biting Wedge
moments.say: I press the small rock down on the tired wedge again.
